recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future Health Canada NPN metadata changes should be handled in THO/UTG, while FHIR core should continue to point implementers to THO instead of maintaining a duplicate national terminology row.
issue_request: FHIR-13404 requested adding http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/ca-hc-npn as the Health Canada Natural Product Number code system URI and also requested http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/ca-hc-npn. The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution accepted adding the URI but noted that national value sets are generally not added to the FHIR specification.
initial_application: svn 14482 / git 54f9e4d added a Health Canada Natural Product Number row for http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/ca-hc-npn to source/terminologies-systems.html. No ca-hc-npn value set was added, consistent with the issue resolution. A later issue, FHIR-30280, corrected the row's OID to 2.16.840.1.113883.5.1107 before later page refactoring removed the row.
additional_context: FHIR-37853 later made HL7 Terminology the authoritative source for external terminology details and removed many external rows, including ca-hc-npn, from the active core Code Systems page. Current source/terminologies-systems.html and source/identifier-registry.html direct readers to HL7 Terminology/THO. THO 7.1.0 contains NamingSystem-v3-hc-npn with the original FHIR URI maintained for backward compatibility and the preferred current CodeSystem URL http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v3-hc-npn; the THO package does not contain a ca-hc-npn ValueSet.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Re-adding the old national external-code-system row or adding the originally requested national value set would conflict with later source-of-truth policy and with FHIR-13404's accepted resolution.

related_jiras.note: Corrected the ca-hc-npn OID after FHIR-13404's initial row used the duplicate DIN OID; already represented on the combined branch.
Moved external terminology authority to THO and removed the ca-hc-npn row from the active core Code Systems page; already represented on the combined branch.
Related Canada discussion about DIN/NPN URI patterns, but it is a separate DIN-focused issue already represented on the combined branch.
Later UTG metadata work for Health Canada code systems and naming systems, confirming that ongoing maintenance belongs in THO/UTG rather than FHIR core.
